svg.title: gov-tla B1 — Constitution.tla: legislation, the Executive and Article V as three machines, each rule a check that TLC shows a property depends on and TLAPS proves
svg.desc: The module models the procedure of Articles I, II and V and Amendments XXII and XXV as three machines over one Executive and one sitting of Congress. Each of its 19 mutations removes one check, and TLC finds a counterexample exactly where the README, the module header and the row list say it should; TLAPS proves each of the thirteen safety properties as Spec => []P under exactly those hypotheses (1,092 obligations). The ten-day rule's liveness, PresentedBillsResolve, is checked, not proved, and the 14 witnesses are checked, never proved. This models the text's procedure: an exercise, not law (README, opening).

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. A witness is checked, never proved. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked). This is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

text.tspan: The three machines over one Executive and one sitting of Congress (README §

svg.text: The module is three machines over one Executive and one sitting of Congress: legislation, the Executive with appointments and impeachment, and Article V. Each arrow is an action, numbered within its machine; the key under each machine gives its guards, the mutation that removes each check, and the flag a violating step would raise.
Congress sits and adjourns as one body; Init has it sitting. Adjourn ends every recess commission (Constitution.tla Adjourn).
Read only where the text turns on a sitting: whether a bill can be returned (Veto, BecomeLawUnsigned, PocketVeto) and whether the Senate is in Recess (
RecessAppoint). Every other act of Congress may happen while it is adjourned (header, Sessions).
Always on: no row empties it. "Legislation reads only the President's presence and the session, and Article V reads nothing" (rows header).
NoOne marks a vacancy; Sign, Veto, Nominate, NominateVP and RecessAppoint need president # NoOne.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars; Next is the disjunction of every action below, with Convene and Adjourn.
FairSpec == Spec /\ TimeRuns (weak fairness on Lapse(b)); SpecPresidentActs == Spec /\ PresidentActs (on Sign(b) \/ Veto(b)). The checked

text.tspan: Key: the actions and the checks they carry

svg.text: 1 Introduce(b, c): MayOriginate, revenue bills start in the House, M_ORIGIN (Art. I §7 cl. 1).
2 PassChamber(b, c, ayes) ×2: a majority of House c, the House of origin first; presented only when BothHouses have passed it, M_UNICAMERAL (cl. 2).
4 BecomeLawUnsigned(b): the ten days run out (Lapse) while Congress sits, M_NO_POCKET; flag tenDayBreach.
5 Veto(b): a President sits and Congress can receive the return (inSession).
6 PocketVeto(b): the ten days run out while Congress is adjourned (Lapse), M_POCKET_SITTING; flag tenDayBreach.
7 Override(b, c, ayes) ×2: origin first; OverrideCarries, two-thirds of House c, M_OVR_VOTE (flag shortOverride); law when OverrideComplete, both Houses, M_OVR_ONE_HOUSE.
8 FailOverride(b): a veto not overridden dies.
Properties its rows read: Bicameralism, Origination, Presentment, TenDayRule.
abstracted: "the whole electoral process in one step"

text.tspan: Key: the actions and the checks they carry

svg.text: 1 Elect(p, v): p, v \in Eligible; Qualified M_DQ, Compatible M_INCOMPAT, TwoPersons M_ONE_PERSON, TermAllowed M_XXII (Art. II §1, Amend. XII, XXII).
2 PresidentVacates: death or resignation; the Vice President becomes President (XXV §1). VicePresidentVacates empties the second seat.
3 NominateVP(p): the Vice Presidency vacant, a President sitting; Qualified, Compatible, TwoPersons(p, president) (XXV §2).
4 ConfirmVP(hAyes, sAyes): re-checks disqualification, M_VP_RECHECK; HouseConfirms, a House majority, M_XXV_SENATE (flag vpWithoutHouse); a Senate majority. RejectVP clears the
5 Nominate(o, p): the office vacant or held by a recess appointee; Qualified, Compatible (Art. II §2 cl. 2).
6 Consent(o, ayes): re-checks disqualification, M_CONSENT_RECHECK; a Senate majority. Reject(o) clears; OfficerResigns(o) vacates.
7 RecessAppoint(o, p): SenateInRecess, M_PRO_FORMA (flag recessWhileSitting); the commission ends at the next Adjourn (cl. 3).
8 Impeach(p, ayes): Impeachable, officeholders only, M_BLOUNT; a House majority (Art. I §2 cl. 5).
9 Convict(p, ayes, dq): ConvictionCarries, two-thirds of the Senate, M_CONVICT_VOTE (flag shortConviction); disqualified if dq. Acquit(p) clears (Art. I §3 cl. 6–7).
10 removal: RemovedBy removes the convicted from every office, the Vice President succeeding a removed President, M_NO_REMOVAL (Art. II §4).
Properties its rows read: Incompatibility, CongressNotImpeachable, ConvictionTwoThirds, TwoTermLimit, Disqualification, PresidentNotVP, XXVBothHouses,
Apply (2) and ratify (3) as a count, n \in StateVotes; which States is abstracted to how many (header,

svg.text: 1 ProposeByCongress(a, hAyes, sAyes): two-thirds of both Houses.
2 ProposeByConvention(a, n): on the application of two-thirds of the States.
3 Ratify(a, n): Ratifies, three-fourths of the States, M_RATIFY_VOTE, and every State for an
No mutation removes a proposal threshold (Mutations).

text.tspan: , as the module header states them (

svg.text: Art. I s.7 cl.2 no bill is presented to the President, so none becomes law, unless both Houses passed it. (Strengthened: it used to say only that a law passed both Houses; it now says it of every presented, returned or enacted bill, which makes it
inductive. It implies the old statement.)
Art. I s.7 cl.1 bills for raising revenue originate in the House.

Art. I s.7 cl.2 every law was signed, or became law unreturned, or was repassed over the veto by both Houses, each by two-thirds (flag shortOverride: an override vote below two-thirds was counted). The two-thirds is new to the property; the old one
Art. I s.7 cl.2, last sentence an unreturned bill is law if Congress sits when the ten days run out, and dies only if adjournment prevents its return (flag tenDayBreach). New.

rests on IncompatPW: Impeach reaches only officeholders, who are not members; hence M_INCOMPAT among its
Art. I s.3 cl.6 no conviction without two- thirds of the Senate (flag shortConviction). New.

Amend. XXII no one is elected President more than twice. (No longer implied by TypeOK: terms is now a function into Nat, not into 0..2.)
Art. I s.3 cl.7 no one disqualified on conviction holds office.
DisqPW: the property pointwise; Convict removes the person it disqualifies from every office
Art. II s.1, Amend. XII, XXV the President and the Vice President are two persons.
PresidentNotVPInv: while a XXV §2 nomination is pending the Vice Presidency is vacant and the nominee is not
Art. V every ratified amendment was ratified by three-fourths of the States, and one touching the Senate's equal suffrage by every State.
Amend. XXV s.2 no Vice President takes office on nomination without a majority of the House as well as of the Senate (flag vpWithoutHouse). New.
a flag, false initially and raised only by one action, whose guard makes the raised value false
Art. II s.2 cl.3 the President fills vacancies alone only during the Recess of the Senate (flag recessWhileSitting). New.
a flag, false initially and raised only by one action, whose guard makes the raised value false

Safety is "the conjunction of the thirteen". The header also lists PresentedBillsResolve, the liveness property: "a bill presented to the President is eventually law, returned, or dead: the ten-day rule."

text.tspan: Art. V — two proposal routes, three-fourths, equal suffrage

svg.text: quorum, Sundays, elections themselves, judicial review, and the age, residency and natural-born tests (folded into the constant Eligible). The ten days on the President's desk are one Lapse step. Congress sits and adjourns as one body, and the session
gates only the return of a bill and recess appointments. An adjourned Congress can still pass a bill, override a veto, confirm a nomination, impeach, hold a trial and propose an amendment.

text.tspan: Abstracted as well, in the module header (ABSTRACTED) but not in the README's paragraph

svg.text: the "more than two years of another's term" nuance of XXII;
presidential succession beyond the Vice President;
votes are counts of ayes, of members or of States; which States ratify or apply is abstracted to how many; ratification and a convention's call are each one step at the moment the count suffices;
a bill that never passes the other House stays pending (no step kills it); one House adjourning without the other (Art. I §5 cl. 4) is not expressed.

All five records agree for every one of the 19 mutations (read when this diagram is built; a disagreement would be drawn as a red row and reported, not reconciled). The theorem column is each …Always theorem whose ASSUME names Mut # "M_X"; the proof module's header says its hypotheses are "exactly the mutations whose rows against P read COUNTEREXAMPLE". A mutation lemma states what the mutation admits; the counterexamples are TLC's (Constitution_proof.tla, MUTATION LEMMAS).
Safety is the conjunction of the thirteen properties in the "Breaks" column. Four of them are new flags (TenDayRule, ConvictionTwoThirds, XXVBothHouses,
RecessAppointmentsInRecess). Three existing ones changed meaning:
Bicameralism now covers every bill presented, returned or enacted.
Presentment now includes two-thirds on each House's override vote.
TwoTermLimit is no longer implied by TypeOK.

An empty cell is a pair no row runs: Safety runs unmutated only. TypeOK runs under each mutation with the machine that mutation changes (rows header). Every COUNTEREXAMPLE cell is one the README's Breaks column and the module header both name, and no HOLDS cell is one they name (read). At one member per House the vote checks are checked only at that size; the theorems cover every size.

Constants set empty (the machine switched off)

svg.text: law by signature, by lapse and by override, and a pocket veto;

A witness's COUNTEREXAMPLE is the expected result: it shows TLC reaches the state the property forbids, so a property that holds is not holding only because that state is unreachable (README § How the specs are written and checked, Witnesses). NeverSuccession and NeverXXVConfirmation are action properties, run as PROPERTY rows (Constitution.tla). TLC does not record a distinct-state count for PROPERTY rows here.

Liveness. FairSpec adds TimeRuns, under which the ten days run out. PresentedBillsResolve holds under FairSpec. It fails under Spec, and under
SpecPresidentActs (fairness on the President instead), because the Presidency can be vacant. NoBehaviour is violated under FairSpec, which shows FairSpec has
a behaviour. No state is terminal.
TimeRuns == \A b \in Bills : WF_vars(Lapse(b)), where Lapse(b) == BecomeLawUnsigned(b) \/ PocketVeto(b): "no one's obligation; the clause
PresidentActs == \A b \in Bills : WF_vars(Sign(b) \/ Veto(b)): "an obligation the text does not impose, stated to show it would not suffice in the clock's
"PresentedBillsResolve, the ten-day rule's leads-to: it is quantified over bills inside the temporal body (\A b : P(b) ~> Q(b)) with an ENABLED premise over b for WF1,
the case for which the pinned prover has no sound route under the writing rules; it is checked by TLC only, in the liveness rows."

text.tspan: Findings about this module (README § Findings; docs/SESSION-GATE-FINDINGS-2026.11.17.md)
A check made at nomination but not at confirmation (README § Findings)

svg.text: "Constitution.tla — a Vice-Presidential nominee could be impeached, convicted and disqualified while pending, then confirmed anyway (M_VP_RECHECK)." TLC found it while the module was first written; it is now a mutation that restores the bug.
The module header: M_VP_RECHECK is "this module's own text before commit fe3ce28, which TLC refuted". Its witness is NeverVPNomineeDisqualified.
"Four actions read inSession, apart from Convene and Adjourn: Veto, BecomeLawUnsigned, PocketVeto and RecessAppoint. Twelve actions of Congress ignore it."

"Nothing checked or proved is wrong": only TenDayRule and RecessAppointmentsInRecess mention the session, and the actions they depend on read it. Government.tla gates Pass and Override on its own inSession; "the two modules disagree".
Recommendation: document the abstraction; "Done in PR #11 (commit 84bd8a1), with the Constitution results regenerated as the 2026.11.18 files", the files drawn here.
